newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bond yields regain some ground in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: NZ bond yields regain some ground in quiet trade.

text.p: 0515 GMT
* NZ bond yields finish slightly stronger
* Money market ends flat
* Pick-up in offshore activity overnight hoped for
* Cash at 9.85 pct vs 9.85 pct on Monday's close
* 90 day bills 9.97 pct vs 9.92 pct
* 7/97 bond yields 8.68 vs 8.66
* 02/01 bond yields 8.19 vs 8.16
* 04/04 bond yields 8.20 vs 8.16
* Sept bill futures 90.13 vs 90.17, vol 1,479
New Zealand bond yields clawed back some of their losses in quiet Tuesday trade but finished short of last night's closing levels.
Short bond yields ended around two points above Monday's close, and longer bonds were off around four, after opening six or seven points weaker on the back of U.S. and Australian weakness.
Ninety day bills and September futures contracts failed to make the same progress, closing on their open at 9.97 percent and 90.13 respectively.

"With the Treasuries falling away again, the market just got a bit of momentum on the negative side, but then domestic institutions started to nibble away and support it," a Wellington bond dealer said.

"Then one of the banks paid the 07/98s reasonably aggressively just before lunch, so that set off rumours about another euro or a samurai, but the currency fell away rather than got bid, so I just don't know how valid that rumour is at the moment," he said.
The Kiwi lost around 20 points to finish at US$0.6925/32.
Any hint of a good rally was curbed by profit-taking in the afternoon and paying interest in the two to three year swap curve.
Dealers said they hoped for more activity in offshore markets overnight with the U.K. back on deck after a bank holiday today.
